Page numbers are the sheet they open on. Part C runs in sidebar order — Overview, Invest, Money, Protect, More — and every screen appears twice, Vault (dark) then Ledger (light), on facing sheets.

The premise

Khazana ships two clients — a Flutter app and this Next.js web app — over one token system. This document specifies the web client, whose 28 routes are a superset of the Flutter app's 24.

Nothing here is a screenshot. Every artboard is redrawn from the same design tokens the app compiles, so a value in this document and a value in globals.css cannot disagree — a build-time check asserts it.

Two named themes
Vault
The dark theme. Four surface levels, borders instead of shadows.
Ledger
The light theme. One subtle shadow; cards are the brightest surface.

Only colour changes between them. Spacing, type, sizing and layout are identical — which is why one artboard source renders both frames in this document.

The governing rule
Emerald = interaction.
Gold = identity.
Gold carries the mark and wealth-flavoured moments and is never a button colour. Making gold the interaction colour is what turns a premium product into a gold-painted generic one.

Card padding20px

Scale

Desktop artboards are drawn at their true 1440 px width and printed at 82% to leave room for the annotation rail. Every measurement quoted in this document is the true value, never the printed one. Mobile artboards are printed 1:1 at 390 px.

Truncation

A frame shows the screen's composition down to a fixed artboard height, the way a Figma frame does. Lists that continue below the cut are shown with their real leading rows — the count in the rail states the full number.

Legend
  1. 1Frame label. Screen name, platform, theme, and the route it serves.
  2. 2Artboard. The redrawn screen on its true theme canvas, clipped to the frame.
  3. 3Callout badge. Anchored to an element, not floated over a coordinate.
  4. 4Annotation rail. Purpose, numbered notes, and a spec table of the values that matter.

Data

Every figure in every frame comes from the demo vault in lib/sampleData.ts — the same one the Settings screen loads. Net worth ₹5.24 Cr, 24 holdings, 3 accounts, 3 liabilities, 3 policies, 5 goals, 91 days of snapshots. Part F prints it in full.

Not investment advice
Figures shown are demonstration data for interface design. The product's own narrative engine carries the same disclaimer and a banned-phrase list that keeps generated copy out of advice territory — see Part E.

Emerald = interaction.
Gold = identity.
Gold carries the mark and wealth-flavoured moments. It is deliberately never a button colour — making gold the interaction colour is what turns a premium product into a gold-painted generic one.
Four surface levels

Jumping from near-black straight to a bright card is what makes dark UI look flat. Vault steps evenly instead:

#080D0B
#101714
#151E1A
#1A2520
The gold text exception
--gold on card
3.9:1 — graphics only
--gold-ink on card
5.2:1 — body text

On Vault, gold already reads 9.4:1, so --gold-ink resolves to the same value. The token exists so no call site has to know which theme it is in.

Success is the interaction colour

A gain and a primary action share one emerald, by decision. The cost is that a profit figure and a button read alike; the benefit is one unambiguous brand green instead of two competing ones.

Asset groups — 14 types collapse to 7

Fourteen categorical hues cannot be kept colourblind-safe, so the asset types roll up to seven groups with a fixed render order. Charts must never sort these slices by value.

An instrument the bundled master does not cover takes the neutral, never a series colour. A grey slice reads as “not known”; a coloured one reads as a real category.

Series colours are fixed hexes, not tokens — a slice must not change identity when the theme does. What changes around them is the track, the legend ink and the 1px separator between arcs, all of which resolve from the theme.

Why the order is frozen

The sequence was validated with a six-check dataviz pass in both themes. Reordering it breaks the guarantee, because the checks are on adjacent pairs — which slices touch is what a reader actually has to separate.

Worst adjacent pair, protanopiaΔE 8.1 ≥ 8
Normal-vision floorΔE 18.2 ≥ 15
Contrast on both groundsall ≥ 3:1 pass
Series count8
Asset groups7
The amber that was dropped

The original brief listed an amber slice beside gold. Under normal vision they are ΔE 14.8 apart — below the 15 floor — so no reader could separate those two slices. The amber was removed rather than shipped as a near-duplicate.

DROPPED
Chart colour is never the only cue

Every coloured mark in the product is paired with a label, a glyph or a sign: donuts carry a legend, deltas carry an arrow, diverging bars carry a centre rule. Colour is the fast read, never the only one.

Proportional — what it would look like
₹2,41,38,144

The 1s narrow and the column ragged-edges. In a finance product that is not a nicety — it is a misread waiting to happen.

One family

Inter across both clients — bundled as four static weights in Flutter, loaded with the optical-size axis on web. There is no second display face: a display serif is reserved for marketing, and shipping one for six letters of wordmark would cost a font request for nothing.

Weights in use
400 Regular — body
500 Medium — labels
600 Semibold — emphasis, buttons
700 Bold — headings, figures
Negative tracking

Display, h1 and h2 tighten (−0.04 to −0.025em). Inter at large sizes reads loose by default, and a headline that has not been tracked in is the clearest tell of an untuned interface. Body text takes a much smaller −0.006em; anything more hurts at 14px.

Radius is prescribed per component

“Everything is a giant rounded rectangle” is the generic look this system avoids: a button is tighter than a card, a card is tighter than a modal.

Elevation is theme-specific
Vault — borders, no shadows
A drop shadow on a near-black canvas is invisible, and faking depth with a glow is what makes finance UI look like a crypto exchange.
Only true overlays get one — --shadow-3.
Ledger — one subtle shadow
The page is #F5F7F5 and the card is #FFFFFF, so a card is the brightest surface. That one step gives depth before a shadow is involved.
Hover lifts to --shadow-2 and −2px.
Motion — one curve, three durations
cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)

One easing curve for the entire product. Standard material easing: quick to leave, slow to settle. A second curve buys nothing and costs consistency.

150ms
--dur-fast
Colour, border, opacity
250ms
--dur
Transform, layout
400ms
--dur-slow
Entrance, chart draw
Reduced motion

Under prefers-reduced-motion every duration collapses to 0.001ms and the hover lift is removed outright. Nothing is merely shortened — the transform itself is dropped.

The mark is the supplied artwork — a rendered gold hexagon with a keyhole and a K — not a redrawn approximation. Because it is raster it is used at 24px and above; below that the bevel and keyhole stop resolving, so the favicon set is pre-composited on the Vault plate at each exact size rather than scaled in the browser.

Why three

Primary — emerald fill, the one action a screen most wants. Secondary — bordered, everything else. Ghost — no chrome, tertiary and in-table. soft and danger are kept as aliases so forty existing call sites did not have to change in one commit: soft maps to secondary, and danger is secondary tinted rather than a fourth shape.

Emerald is the interaction colour

Gold never lands on a button. On Vault the fill is #20C98A with near-black ink at 9.4:1; white on that emerald would be 2.4:1.

Height36px
Padding0 14px
Radius9px
Type13px / 600 / −0.01em
Icon gap8px
Transition150ms standard
ActivetranslateY(1px)
Disabledopacity 0.4, no press
Focus ring2px canvas + 2px accent-line
Delta carries an arrow

Colour alone fails for a colourblind reader and in print, so the glyph repeats the information: ↑ up, ↓ down, · flat. A null value renders an em dash in muted ink — never a zero, which would assert a fact the vault does not have.

Chip tones are semantic

Each tone is a soft background, a matching ink, and a border mixed from the same token at 26–30% — so a chip holds its shape on any of the four surface levels.

Progress zones

Under 70% success, 70–90% warning, over 90% danger — derived from the fraction, never stored. The same function drives budget tiles, credit utilisation, coverage gaps and the transactions rail, so two bars showing the same ratio can never disagree.

Banners are not toasts

They sit in the layout and persist. Nothing important in this product is announced by something that disappears on a timer.

One card, divided

The KPI row is a single card split by hairlines, not four cards. Four separate cards read as four sections and compete with the real sections below them.

A monogram plate, not a logo. Two letters at 700 on --fill, 11px radius at 32px and above, 9px below. Tinted by semantics where the type matters — success wash for income, violet for transfers.

Truncation is deliberate

Every cell truncates rather than wraps. A table whose rows change height as data changes cannot be scanned, and in a ledger scanning is the whole job.

Shared rules

Every chart takes its colours from tokens, draws its grid from --grid-line, and labels its axes in --muted at 10.5px. None of them renders a tooltip through the title attribute — an OS tooltip waits a second, is styled by the platform, and never appears on a touch screen at all.

Donut thickness18–22px
Donut gap0.014 rad
Donut track--fill-strong
Area stroke2px, non-scaling
Area fill26% → 0% gradient
Grid lines3, at 25/50/75%
Column width12px
Column radius4px top
Column gap2px
Bar height9px
Ring stroke9–11px, round cap
Gauge sweep240°
Gauge stroke15px
Band arc3.5px at 30%
Order, not sorting

Asset-group donuts render in the fixed group order. Sorting slices by value would reshuffle which hues sit adjacent, and adjacency is exactly what the colourblind validation was run against.

Entrance

Lines draw in via stroke-dashoffset, bars grow from the baseline via scaleY, rings and gauges animate stroke-dashoffset over 600ms. All are suppressed entirely under reduced motion — see Part E.

What this screen is for

The one screen that answers “where do I stand”. Seven headline figures, then the net-worth trend, allocation, movers, health, generated insights, top positions and what is due next — in that order, because it descends from position to trajectory to detail.

Annotations
  1. 1KPI strip. One card, divided by hairlines rather than seven cards — a row of separate cards competes with the sections below it. Figures are 22px/700 at −0.035em tracking, tabular.
  2. 2Portfolio performance. Reads the real 91-day snapshot series. With fewer than two snapshots the app draws a labelled derived estimate instead of an empty chart.
  3. 3Allocation. Segmented control switches the roll-up dimension between asset group, sector and market cap. Any roll-up must sum exactly to the portfolio total.
  4. 4Health gauge. 240° sweep with the five bands drawn faintly on the track. Below 50% tracked weight the grade renders null, not a low score.
  5. 5Insights. Generated sentences filtered through a banned-phrase list (“consider”, “you should”, “invest in”) and always closed by the disclaimer.
  6. 6Top holdings. Six rows of the 24; the link states the full count so the truncation is never mistaken for the whole book.

What this screen is for

Structural questions the Dashboard deliberately does not answer: how concentrated the book is, how returns are spread across positions, and where value actually sits once you drill past the asset group.

Annotations
  1. 1Scores, not verdicts. Diversification, concentration and return quality are indices over the book. When an input is missing the screen renders null — a dash — rather than a zero that would read as a real, terrible score.
  2. 2Diversification gauge. Same 240° component as the health screen, different domain, so a reader who has learned one dial has learned both.
  3. 3Return distribution. A count histogram, not a value one: the question is how many positions are working, which a value-weighted chart would hide behind the largest holding.
  4. 4Sunburst. Asset group inner ring, positions outer. Outer-ring opacity steps down by rank inside the group rather than introducing new hues, which would break the palette.
Spec
Gauge sweep240°
Gauge stroke15px
Sunburst inner r0.20 × size
Sunburst outer r0.46 × size
Bar radius4px top
Column gap2px

Net worth trend

What this screen is for

The accounting view. Twelve months of income against spending, where the money went, and a balance sheet assembled from the double-entry postings rather than from summed transactions.

Annotations
  1. 1Savings rate is income less spending over income, on the same window as the figures beside it — never a different period, which is the usual way this number lies.
  2. 2Two-series columns. Income and expenses share a group with a 2px gap; the surface showing through is the separator, so no third colour is introduced.
  3. 3Balance sheet. Built from postings, and the header states whether assets less liabilities less equity nets to zero within ₹0.005. Transfers never appear here — they are not income or expense, and the ledger keeps them out.
Spec
Column width12px
Column radius4px 4px 0 0
Bar height9px
Balanced tolerance₹0.005
Window12 months

What this screen is for

The investment home. Six headline figures, then allocation read three ways, the extremes of the book, and every position in one table. The route keeps its old /investments path because it is one of the five Flutter tabs — only the label moved.

Annotations
  1. 1Six KPIs, not seven. Portfolio screens answer value, cost, total return and today's return first; count and quantity are context, so they sit last.
  2. 2Three donuts, one grammar. Asset group keeps the fixed palette order; sector and profit-split may sort by value because both are labelled in the legend beside them.
  3. 3Diverging P&L. Sign is the message, so the bars grow from a centre rule rather than from a left edge — magnitude and direction in one read.
  4. 4Holdings table. Numeric columns are right-aligned and tabular so digits line up column-wise; only the instrument column is left-aligned.

Why prices are typed

Khazana never calls a market data feed on its own. A price is here because you entered it, or because you pasted a broker export. That is the whole privacy contract: no request leaves the device carrying a list of what you own.

Add a price provider
Settings → Market data lets you supply your own API key. The key is stored in the OS keychain, never in the vault.
Open market data settings
What this screen is for

Instruments tracked but not owned, with a target price and the distance to it. Prices are hand-entered; nothing on this screen calls out to a market feed.

Annotations
  1. 1To target reuses the Delta component. A negative distance means the price has passed the target — the arrow says so without the reader parsing the sign.
  2. 2The privacy panel is design, not documentation. Explaining the missing live feed on the screen that most invites the question is what stops it reading as a broken feature.

Row actions14px icons, muted
Avatar26px, 9px radius
Empty targetrenders “—”

What this screen is for

Index levels and the day's movement across your book. The only screen in the product that shows figures Khazana generated rather than figures you entered — which is why the demonstration badge sits in the page header, not in a footnote.

Annotations
  1. 1Demo badge in the title row. Warning tone, always visible, never dismissible on this screen. Synthesised numbers that look like a live feed are the most damaging thing a finance UI can ship quietly.
  2. 2Day change never blends. If one real previous close exists in the vault, every synthesised day change is dropped rather than mixed with it.
  3. 3The session clock is real. Market hours come from the device, so “open” is true even though the level beside it is not.

This is the identical mockup source as the preceding sheet with one class changed. Spacing, type, sizing and layout are byte-identical; only the palette resolves differently.

What changes

Why the emerald darkens

#20C98A on a white card reads 2.1:1 — unusable for text or a small mark. Ledger steps the same hue down to #087A56 (5.6:1) and pairs it with white, while Vault keeps the bright step against near-black ink at 9.4:1. The two are the same brand colour at the lightness each background can carry.

Unrealised positions only, FIFO lots, no set-off against carried-forward losses. Informational only — not tax advice.
What this screen is for

What the book would cost in capital-gains tax if it were realised today, position by position, under the India FY25 rules bundled with the app.

Annotations
  1. 1Long / short is computed, not chosen. Holding period against the per-asset-type threshold decides the term; the chip states which side each position fell on.
  2. 2Slab-rated positions show “Slab” rather than a number, because the rate depends on income the app does not know. Inventing 30% here would be a confident wrong answer.
  3. 3The rules panel is versioned. Schema version and effective date are on screen, so a figure can always be traced to the rule set that produced it.
Spec
Rule sourceassets/tax_rules.json v4
Effective2024-07-23
Lot methodFIFO, not configurable
LTCG exemption₹1,25,000

A transfer is neither income nor expense. Budgets and Reports are blind to these rows by design.

What this screen is for

Where money is held. Balances come from double-entry postings, not from summing transactions — which is what lets a transfer move value without inventing income.

Annotations
  1. 1Balance is derived. Opening balance plus postings. If the postings were ever missing, every account here would read as its opening balance — the Diagnostics screen checks for exactly that.
  2. 2Account cards, not rows. Three accounts fit as cards and each carries its own actions; the pattern degrades to a table past about eight.
  3. 3Transfers are violet. Neither income green nor expense red, because a transfer is neither — and Budgets and Reports ignore them entirely.
Spec
Account avatar42px, 11px radius
Balance type21px / 700
Card actionsghost buttons, 36px
Transfer tonevar(--violet)

What this screen is for

The ledger. One timeline over expenses, income and transfers, grouped by day with a running net per day, plus the budget strip and the capture queue alongside.

Annotations
  1. 1Day headers carry the day's net. Scanning a month is a sequence of daily nets; making the reader add rows to get there is the most common failure of a transaction list.
  2. 2Category avatars are tinted by type — success wash for income, violet for transfers, neutral fill for spending — so the type is legible before the amount is read.
  3. 3Signs, not just colour. A plus or a minus precedes every amount, because colour alone fails for a colourblind reader and in print.
Spec
Row height~50px
Avatar34px, 11px radius
Day header11px / 700 / 0.06em
Amount type13.5px / 600, tabular

What this screen is for

The same ledger on a month grid. Useful for the question a list answers badly — when in the month does money actually leave.

Annotations
  1. 1Cells carry both figures. Income above expense, compact form, tabular. A single net number per day would hide a heavy day that happened to balance.
  2. 2Future days are dimmed to 42%, not hidden — the shape of the month stays intact while nothing suggests data exists where it does not.
  3. 3Below 600px the grid collapses to a single column and the day detail becomes a bottom sheet; the desktop layout keeps it as a persistent right-hand panel.

What this screen is for

Savings targets with progress rings, deadlines and the monthly contribution each one implies. A goal can be linked to an account, in which case its progress is that balance.

  1. 1Ring, not bar. A goal is one number against one target with no zones — the ring reads as a single completion, and it distinguishes goals from budgets at a glance.

  1. 1Renewals inside 30 days become a danger chip on the policy itself, and the same window drives the notification menu in the topbar.
  2. 2Gap rules are printed beside the bars. “10 × annual income” is a stated assumption a reader can disagree with, not a black-box target.
  3. 3Untracked ≠ uncovered. Vehicle and home cover are absent from the gap panel rather than shown at zero, and the note says why.

What this screen is for

Bulk entry from a broker or bank export. Three steps — choose a source, preview every parsed row, confirm — with an undo that is scoped to the batch.

Annotations
  1. 1Preview is the whole feature. The result of each row is stated before anything is written: new, updates existing, or rejected with the reason.
  2. 2Rejections are shown, not dropped. A symbol missing from the instrument master fails loudly here rather than appearing later as an “Unclassified” slice.
  3. 3Undo is per batch. It removes exactly the records that import created and leaves anything edited since alone.

Why this is synthetic

A real news feed means a request to a server, and a request from this app would carry the shape of what you hold. The product's core promise is that no such request exists — so the feed is generated locally and labelled as generated.

Twelve fixed headlines
Deterministic, offline, and badged everywhere they appear.

How alerts fire

Rules are evaluated when the app is open and prices change — there is no background service and no push. An armed rule with a stale price stays armed rather than firing on old data.

What this screen is for

Price and weight rules, evaluated locally against the prices in your vault. Armed rules show how far the current value sits from the threshold.

  3. 3No background service. Rules evaluate when the app is open; the panel says so, because a user who expects a push notification and does not get one has been misled by the UI.

Help SS Personal Self Search transactions, holdings… ⌘K NSE open · 27,412.35 SS

Help

How Khazana works, and what it promises

1

How it works

Your PIN is the key
The PIN derives an AES-256 key. It is never stored, never transmitted, and cannot be recovered — which is the point. Lose it and the vault is unreadable, including to us.
Double-entry underneath
Every transaction writes balanced postings. That is why account balances, the balance sheet and net worth always agree, and why a transfer moves money without inventing income.
You supply the prices
Holdings are priced by what you enter or import. No feed is called on your behalf, because a request for your holdings is a disclosure of your holdings.
Backups are portable
An encrypted .ftos file restores into the mobile app and back. Both clients share the format, so neither can hold your data hostage.
2

Keyboard

⌘K Command palette
N New transaction
⌘L Lock the vault
G then D Go to dashboard
/ Focus search

Take the tour

Thirteen pages covering the vault, the ledger, the portfolio and the score.

Start the tour
3

Deliberately absent

No account or sign-in
No cloud sync service
No live market feed
No advice or recommendations
No analytics of any kind
What this screen is for

How the product works and what it deliberately does not do — the four mechanisms a user has to trust, and an explicit list of the absences.

Annotations
  1. 1Mechanism, not FAQ. Four explanations of how the thing actually works beat twenty questions nobody asked.
  2. 2“Deliberately absent” is a list. Naming what the product will not do is what stops each absence being read as an unfinished feature.
Spec
Explainer row~104px
Icon plate40px, accent wash
Keycap6px radius, fill-strong
Tour13 pages

These five match the Flutter app's bottom bar exactly, and a test asserts the two lists stay in step. A user moving between clients should not have to relearn where things are. /investments keeps its path for that reason — only its label became “Portfolio”.

Grouping is not decoration

At twenty-plus destinations a flat list stops being scannable. The five groups answer “what am I trying to do” — look at it, grow it, spend it, protect it, everything else — rather than mirroring the data model, which would have put Holdings under a different heading from Portfolio.

Sidebar destinations26
Groups5
Phone tabs5
Off-nav routes/add · / (redirect)
Web-only screens10
Flutter-only screens2 — Capture Inbox, Market data
Every route is in the sidebar

No destination is reachable only by a link from another screen. A guarded test walks NAV_ITEMS against the route table, so a new page that forgets to register itself fails the build rather than becoming orphaned.

Depth is two, everywhere

Sidebar → screen. Nothing nests a third level; where a screen needs detail it uses a segmented control, a drawer or a row expansion rather than a sub-route. The one exception is /add, which is modal and returns to where it was opened from.

Cross-client parity
Flutter screens24
Web routes28
Shared18
Flutter nav5 tabs · 19-item desktop sidebar
Shared tokenscolour · type · space · motion
Shared algorithmshealth · safety net · tax · FIFO
Shared fixturehealth_cases.json, byte-identical

Web-only: Holdings, Watchlist, Markets, Dividends, Tax Center, Reconcile, News, Alerts, Diagnostics, Help. Flutter-only: Capture Inbox (SMS review) and Market Data settings.

The gate is the only blocking step. Everything after it is skippable — a user who wants an empty vault gets one, and the demo badge appears only if they choose the sample.

Add a transaction the highest-frequency path in the product
Trigger
FAB · sidebar button · N key
Amount
52px field, focused on open
Category
One tap from an 11-tile grid
Details
Merchant remembered from history
Save
Writes txn + balanced postings

Quick add short-circuits the middle three: “1240 swiggy food today” is parsed on device and shown as chips before anything is written. Budget impact is displayed while the entry can still be reconsidered.

Import a broker file the only bulk write path
Choose source
10 institution presets
Parse
Read locally — never uploaded
Preview
Every row labelled new / update / reject
Confirm
One batch id recorded
Undo
Removes exactly that batch

Rejected rows are shown with a reason rather than dropped silently — a symbol missing from the instrument master would otherwise surface later as an “Unclassified” slice.

Reconcile an account proving the book is true
Pick account
and enter the statement balance
Tick entries
Cleared balance updates live
Difference
Warning tone — not an error
Explain
App names entries that would close the gap
Finish
Cleared flags persist

The app never ticks anything on the user's behalf. It narrows the search and stops — an auto-reconciled book is a book nobody has actually checked.

Lock and ghost the shoulder-surfing path
Working
Vault unlocked
Ghost mode
Every figure masked as ••••••
Idle
Auto-lock timer, default 5 min
Locked
Key discarded from memory
Unlock
PIN or platform biometrics

Ghost mode and lock are different tools: ghost keeps the session alive for a screen share, lock destroys the in-memory key. ⌘L is bound to the second.

One rule across all five

Nothing is written until the user confirms it. Import previews, capture drafts sit in a queue, reconcile ticks are manual, quick-add shows its parse as chips. The product never acts on an inference and reports it afterwards.

Reversibility
Importundo, per batch
Transactionedit or delete
Capture draftconfirm or dismiss
Reconcileuntick freely
Sample dataidempotent reload
Erase vaultirreversible
Lost PINirreversible

Exactly two actions cannot be undone, and both say so in the flow that reaches them rather than in a support article found afterwards.

Entry points to Add

FAB on Overview and Cash Flow, the sidebar's primary button, the N shortcut, the command palette, and “Add for this day” on the calendar. Five doors to one destination is correct for the action a user takes fifty times a week.

What has no flow

There is no onboarding wizard, no account recovery, no sync setup and no notification permission prompt. Each of those is absent because the corresponding feature is absent — Part F lists them.

Part E · UX Motion & interaction One curve, three durations globals.css keyframes
WhatBehaviourKeyframeDurationEasingNotes
Page entranceContent rises 10px and fades in kz-rise 400msstandardStaggered 40ms per card, capped at 6
Card hovertranslateY(−2px) + shadow-2 — 250msstandardOpt-in via .lift; removed under reduced motion
Button presstranslateY(1px) — instant—No duration — a press must feel immediate
Button colourBackground, border, ink — 150msstandardFast enough to feel attached to the cursor
Focus ring2px canvas + 2px accent-line — 150msstandardNever suppressed, in any theme
Line chartstroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 kz-draw 400msstandardDraws left to right on mount only
Bars / columnsscaleY 0 → 1 from the baseline kz-grow 400msstandardOpacity 0.4 → 1 alongside
Progress barwidth transition — 500msstandardLonger, because the value is the message
Ring / gaugestroke-dashoffset — 600msstandardThe slowest thing in the product
SegmentedBackground and ink swap — 150msstandardThe thumb does not slide — it swaps
Drawer / sheetSlide from edge + scrim fade — 250msstandardScrim is the only place blur is used
Command paletteScale 0.98 → 1 + fade — 150msstandardFast: it is a keyboard tool
Hover

Cards lift 2px and gain a shadow. Rows tint with --fill. Buttons move to their hover token. Nothing scales, and nothing changes size — a layout that reflows on hover is a layout that cannot be pointed at.

Focus

A two-part ring: 2px of the canvas colour, then 2px of --accent-line. The inner ring is what keeps it legible against a card and against a filled button. :focus-visible, so a mouse click does not draw it.

Pressed

One pixel down, no transition. Every other state animates; this one must not, because a delayed press response is the single clearest way to make an interface feel broken.

Reduced motion

Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every animation and transition drops to 0.001ms, iteration count is forced to 1, smooth scrolling is disabled, and the hover lift is removed rather than shortened. Charts render at their final state immediately — the information was never in the animation.

Keyboard
Command palette⌘K / Ctrl K
New transactionN
Lock vault⌘L / Ctrl L
Focus search/
DismissEsc
Move focusTab / Shift Tab
ActivateEnter / Space
Feedback surfaces

Banners persist in the layout. Confirms are modal and name the consequence in the button (“Erase vault”, not “OK”). There are no toasts — nothing that matters in this product is announced by something that disappears on a timer.

Loading

Local reads finish in single-digit milliseconds, so there are no skeletons on ordinary navigation. The three places that can genuinely wait — unlock, import parse, sample-data load — show a determinate state with a label, never an indefinite spinner.

Why one curve

A second easing curve buys nothing a reader can name and costs consistency across two clients. cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) is quick to leave and slow to settle, which suits every transition in the product.

Every screen has six states
StateTreatmentWhere it comes from
PopulatedThe artboards in Part CVault has records
EmptyEmptyState — icon plate, one line, one actionNew vault, or a filter with no matches
PartialMissing values render “—”, never 0; counts state coverageUnpriced holdings, untracked cover
LoadingDeterminate label; no indefinite spinnerUnlock, import parse, sample load
ErrorDanger banner in the layout, with the recovery actionInsecure context, restore failure, parse failure
GhostEvery figure masked as ••••••; layout unchangedUser toggle, for a shared screen
Untracked is not zero
Correct
Home cover
—
Not tracked
Protection score
71
Renormalised over 2 of 3
Wrong
Home cover
₹0
Asserts a fact
Protection score
47
Punishes a gap in knowledge

This is the single most load-bearing display rule in the product. A vault that has not been told about a policy is not a vault with no policy, and a score that treats the two the same is lying with a number.

Generated copy is constrained

Narrative sentences are filtered through a banned-phrase list before they can render, and every insight surface closes with the disclaimer:

buysellinvest inrecommendyou shouldguaranteedconsiderprioritise

“Informational only — not investment advice.” The rule is enforced at the render layer, not in review, because copy written months apart drifts and a compliance boundary that depends on memory is not a boundary.

Accessibility
Body contrast, Vault#F4F7F5 on #151E1A — 14.8:1
Body contrast, Ledger#101613 on #FFFFFF — 17.6:1
Secondary ink≥ 5:1 both themes
Muted ink≥ 4.5:1 both themes
Emerald on card9.4:1 Vault · 5.6:1 Ledger
Gold as textuses --gold-ink, ≥ 5:1
Chart marksall ≥ 3:1 on both grounds
Min touch target48px
Focus indicatoralways visible, never removed
Colour is never alone

Deltas carry an arrow. Amounts carry a sign. Diverging bars carry a centre rule. Chart slices carry a legend. Status carries a labelled chip. Every one of these would survive being printed in greyscale — which this document, on a monochrome printer, actually tests.

Screen readers

Figures expose a spelled-out form via moneyToWords in Indian numbering — “two crore forty-one lakh…” — because a screen reader given ₹2,41,38,144 reads a digit sequence, not a quantity. Charts carry a text summary; decorative SVG is aria-hidden.

Not yet verified

The contrast figures above are computed from the token pairs. A full assistive-technology pass — VoiceOver and NVDA against the live build, keyboard-only traversal of all 28 routes — has not been run, and this document does not claim it has.

Part F · Appendix Contracts, caveats and what is deliberately absent Read before changing anything
Frozen contracts

Three strings cannot change without breaking existing installs or the cross-client backup format. None of them is brand, and none should be “tidied”.

WhatValueWhy
Vault verifierFTOS-OKProves a PIN decrypted correctly
Database namefintech_osRenaming orphans every existing vault
Backup extension.ftosPaired with the Flutter backup magic
Deliberately empty data files
FileWhy
benchmarks.json → seriesIndex close series need licensed data; an invented one would make benchmark comparison confidently wrong
fund_portfolios.json → schemesMF look-through needs real AMC disclosures, so overlap analysis is disabled rather than faked
The one data discrepancy

sampleData.ts backfills ninety days of history ending at a hardcoded ₹5.24 Cr, but the holdings and accounts it seeds compute to ₹2.19Cr. The ledger is right and the backfill is decorative. This document uses the computed figure everywhere and scales the snapshot curve onto it, preserving its shape. It is exactly the class of inconsistency the Diagnostics screen exists to surface — and worth fixing in the seed.

Each of these is a decision, not a gap. Reading them as a backlog is the most likely way to misuse this document.

Account or sign-in
There is no server to hold one
Cloud sync service

Disabled until licensed index data exists
Caveats on this document

The artboards are redrawn from tokens, not screenshots of the running build. They are accurate to the design system and to the demo data; where a shipped screen has drifted from its tokens, this document shows the intent rather than the drift.

It specifies the web client. The Flutter app shares the tokens, the algorithms and the five-tab bar, but its desktop sidebar carries 19 items in four sections and it has two screens the web build does not.

Contrast figures in Part E are computed from token pairs. No assistive-technology pass has been run against the live build, and this document does not claim one.
